$comment: Ship tiers for every [WebSocket] endpoint. This is the ONE hand-maintained input to Build-EndpointInventory.ps1: everything else in endpoint-inventory.json is derived from src/IM.Server. Adding a server endpoint without tiering it here fails the generator on purpose. Rationale for the tier boundaries is sdk/CONTRACT.md §3. 这是生成器唯一的人工输入：新增服务端端点却不在此分层，生成器会刻意失败。

T0.title: Session floor
T0.rule: No client of any shape works without these. They are transport lifecycle, not product features: an SDK that omits one is broken rather than incomplete.

T1.title: 1:1 chat MVP
T1.rule: The smallest set that ships a two-person chat app a customer would actually launch: send, receive, backfill, read state, profiles, attachments, offline push. Cutting any one of these leaves a hole the tenant must fill with raw invoke() on day one.

T2.title: Social graph and groups
T2.rule: What turns a 1:1 chat into a messenger: contacts, blocking, group create/join/manage, presence, and the message operations users expect once more than two people can see a message.

T3.title: Competitive parity
T3.rule: Not needed to ship, needed to win. These are the rows a buyer ticks off against 融云 / 环信 / 网易云信 feature matrices. A tenant can live without each one individually; a buyer comparing tables cannot.

T4.title: Specialist verticals
T4.rule: Load-bearing for a minority of tenants and dead weight for the rest: calls, service desk, end-to-end encryption, live chat rooms, AI streaming, scheduling, folders. Correctly typed when a customer asks; never a reason to delay T0–T3.

conn.heartbeat.note: Cadence is server-owned: obey intervalSeconds from the reply, never a client constant.

conn.reauth.note: Untyped in all five SDKs today. Without it a long-lived session dies at token expiry instead of renewing in place.

conn.sync.note: Cold-start correctness hinges on this call's convSeqs. See sdk/CONTRACT.md §5.

msg.sync.note: Both the gap-repair primitive and a public method: tenants with their own store call it directly.

msg.recall.note: Window is per-tenant (App.Settings.RecallWindowMinutes); expect 1403 outside it.

msg.delete.note: Delete-for-me. Distinct from recall, which withdraws for everyone.

conv.unreadTotal.note: Drives the app badge; a chat app cannot ship a correct badge without it.

user.batchProfile.note: The one that keeps a conversation list from issuing N profile calls.

media.uploadTicket.note: A chat app without images is not shippable, and images cannot be sent without a ticket.

push.register.note: See sdk/CONTRACT.md §6. Registration is a client responsibility on every connect, not a one-time setup step.

push.unregister.note: Logout must call this BEFORE disconnecting; after the socket closes only the tenant backend can remove the token.

push.clicked.note: SPEC-05 §6.2 / SPEC-02 §2.6.3: report a notification tap with { pushId?, messageId? } (messageId is the payload's msgId). Best-effort statistics; identity comes from the socket, never retry on failure.

msg.edit.note: Window is App.Settings.EditWindowMinutes; expect 1405 outside it.

msg.receipt.note: Per-message delivered/read marks, distinct from the conversation read pointer in conv.read.

conv.setting.note: Pin, mute, draft and tags in one call.

user.subscribePresence.note: NOT gated by EnablePresence server-side, unlike user.presence: a subscribe on a presence-disabled app succeeds and then never fires. SDKs must not infer the flag from this call.

friend.block.note: App-store review treats user blocking as mandatory for any app with user-generated content.

moderation.report.note: The other half of what friend.block is here for: app-store review requires both a way to block an abusive user and a way to report objectionable content. An SDK that has completed T2 without this still cannot pass review, which is the same argument that put blocking in T2.

msg.receiptDetail.note: Group read-by list; server caps it at App.Settings.ReceiptGroupMemberLimit.

msg.search.note: Off by default (EnableSearch defaults false) and separately rate limited with 1003.

msg.burn.note: Burn-after-reading. Widely expected in the CN market this product competes in.

msg.translate.note: IM.Modules.Ai; returns 1203 when no provider is configured.

msg.streamBegin.note: Streaming assistant replies. Pairs with the evt.stream push.

room.join.note: Chat rooms are best-effort and carry seq 0: they must bypass the gap-repair path entirely.

call.invite.note: IM.Modules.Calls; signalling only, the SDK never carries media.

desk.request.note: Agent-console surface. The customer side of a desk session arrives as ordinary messages.

desk.rate.note: The customer rates a finished desk session. Tiered on 2026-08-27: it shipped untiered, which stopped the generator and froze the inventory.

desk.suggest.note: LLM reply suggestions for an agent; returns 1203 when no provider is configured. Tiered on 2026-08-27 with desk.rate and desk.canned.

desk.canned.note: The agent's canned-reply list. Its request body is optional, which is what the generator's parameter regex could not read until 2026-08-27.

keys.publish.note: E2EE key directory. The SDK stores and transports keys; it performs no cryptography.
